rules.statement: A change with escalations publishes only after a person other than its author, holding cosec:approve on the document, approves the candidate digest they saw.
guards: control:ControlAuthorizationTest#what the analysis cannot prove waits for another person's approval of its digest
control:StoredApprovalTest#a stored approval counts only when another person approved the candidate published

rules.statement: An approval is valid for cosec.control.approval.expire-after (72 hours); an expired one publishes nothing and the change awaits approval again.
guards: control:ControlAuthorizationTest#an expired approval publishes nothing and asks again

rules.statement: A holder of cosec:approve on the document in the platform tenant is the trust root: its own changes are not analyzed and need no second person, unless four-eyes is on, when what the analysis cannot prove needs another holder, a platform principal too. A tenant principal holding cosec:approve is not the trust root: its own changes are analyzed (RC1-10). A workload is never the trust root: a principal whose credential declares itself a workload's (an API key's and a service's own identity are by construction, IDN-34), one with no credential, or one CoSec's API key authenticator proved (IDN-44).
guards: control:ApprovalB2Test#a tenant approver's own change is analyzed, and it approves others' - RC1-10
control:ControlAuthorizationTest#the trust root publishes alone unless four-eyes is on
control:ApprovalB2Test#under four-eyes a platform principal's change needs a platform approver
control:ApprovalB2Test#an API key is never the trust root - review M2
control:ApprovalB2Test#a service's own identity is never the trust root - IDN-34

rules.statement: A new or changed break-glass binding always needs a second person's approval, whoever proposes it.
guards: control:BreakGlassControlTest#two people create it, each step recorded first
control:LiveBreakGlassChangeTest#changing a live binding needs a second person too

rules.statement: An approval records every token attribute of its approver, whatever its JSON type, and publishing checks the approver's cosec:approve again with exactly those attributes.
guards: control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#an approval keeps every attribute of its approver, so that publishing checks what it was decided on
control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#an approval's other attribute types survive the store

rules.statement: A change of an app document that adds or widens an ALLOW of a permission policy names the tenant documents the back-reference index lists as binding that policy in the app, as one informational entry per policy (CTL-48), without reading a tenant document; the entry never stands in for the escalation the widening needs (the change also carries NOT_ANALYZED), so a person still approves it.
guards: control:ChangesB1Test#widening an app permission policy lists the tenant bindings it widens - RC1-34

rules.statement: An approval is a person's: a principal authenticated by a workload's credential (an API key, or a service's own identity, IDN-34) never approves (403), whatever it holds. A workload is told by the kind its credential declares (IDN-44), a forwarded identity's `auth.kind` among them (absent or unknown, a workload's), by having no credential, and by provenance (CoSec's API key authenticator); never by the method's name.
guards: control:ApprovalB2Test#an API key never approves
control:ApprovalB2Test#an API key is never the trust root - review M2
runtime:ApiKeyAuthenticatorTest#aValidKeyIsItsPrincipal
runtime:IdentityGateTest#the gateway's credential decides principal and break-glass bindings behind it
control:ApprovalB2Test#a service's own identity never approves - IDN-34

rules.statement: An approval records the approver's token id and issue time; at publish it no longer counts when that token, or every token of the approver issued by then, has been revoked since, nor when it records no token id (made before the upgrade, by an older instance, or with a credential without one, which cannot approve at all), nor when the approver's memberships come from the provider and either decision, on the roles it held then and holds now or on what the provider answers now, does not permit. Revocations that cannot be read publish nothing (503).
guards: control:ApprovalB2Test#an approval by a token revoked since does not count
control:ApprovalB2Test#an approver from the provider counts with the roles it holds now
spring-boot:ControlApprovalStarterTest#an approval by a provider-membership token publishes
spring-boot:ControlApprovalStarterTest#an approval by a token revoked since does not publish
control:ControlReviewFixesTest#an approval that cannot be checked again does not count
control:ApprovalB2Test#revocations that cannot be read publish nothing

rules.source: The pre-release review of 8.0.0-beta.9 (findings A-2 and B-1), decided by the coordinator on 2026-11-25; RFC 0007 §7.5
rules.statement: An approval records whose the approver's credential was, its kind (PERSON or WORKLOAD) as the host that recorded it read it, and the change answer shows it (approval.kind). At publication an approval counts only when it says a person's: one that records no kind, as every approval recorded before kinds, or a workload's, does not count, and the change waits for an approval again, its APPROVAL finding saying so. So a workload never approves (APR-7) holds at publication too, whichever version recorded the approval. An older reader that ignores the member reads the person's approval this version recorded; one that drops it in a rewrite leaves an approval that does not count, which narrows.
guards: control:ApprovalKindTest#an approval counts only when it says its approver was a person - APR-9
control:ApprovalKindTest#a stored approval keeps its kind, and one recorded before kinds reads as none - APR-9
control:ControlRoundTwoFixesTest#an approval keeps every attribute of its approver, so that publishing checks what it was decided on
